headline: Committee weighs conditions for Pāʻia Sugar Mill rezoning

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: Members discussed conditions on rezoning the Pāʻia Sugar Mill site, including water rules and open space, before going into recess.
meeting.recap: An applicant asked the committee to approve a rezoning for the Pāʻia Sugar Mill site.[[0:07:28]] A supporting testifier said the zoning would drop from heavy industrial to light industrial.[[0:18:45]] A committee member noted that farm land on the site would also become light industrial.[[0:20:14]] The chair closed spoken testimony, and written testimony is still accepted.[[0:22:01]] A committee member proposed conditions, including water-saving rules, no vacation rentals, and an emergency evacuation route.[[0:25:09]] An applicant said they would "100%" follow best water practices.[[0:26:58]] Planning said that without a deadline, the code would allow five years to build a required facility.[[0:48:37]] Another proposed condition would keep at least 20% of the property as open space forever.[[0:52:49]] Planning said one county department did not review the rezoning.[[0:56:17]] The chair asked staff to send that department a letter before full council review.[[1:00:35]] A committee member urged keeping conditions few and suggested possible tax breaks.[[1:09:56]] The committee went into recess until 11.[[1:18:36]]
meeting.next: The committee can send a letter to Public Works to ask what building code already requires for hurricane standards. Staff will prepare a letter asking the department that did not review the rezoning for its thoughts before full council review. During the recess, a definition or examples of open space may be worked out. The committee will use the recess to discuss wording for the franchise or local business condition. Staff was asked to compare the water rules in effect since March 1 with what was presented in early January.

moments.q: "the community has to be our measure of success"
Chair reads back the proposed conditions
Question on why one department did not review the rezoning
"We are 100% supportive for the true history from the beginning."

issues.oneLine: Planning asked whether the council is okay with the workforce housing the applicants described, so a condition does not block it.
issues.why: Planning said that otherwise the applicants might have to seek other relief to build housing.
issues.brief: A testifier said the larger plan includes workforce housing.[[#1]] A committee member said she supports living facilities but not short-term transient rentals.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: A committee member proposed an ag processing facility, such as a community commercial kitchen, as a condition.
issues.why: The member said ag processing on site would support resilience in hard times.
issues.next: The chair said a recess would be used to discuss wording for the proposed conditions.
issues.brief: An applicant said they want to have a commercial kitchen at the site.[[#1]] A speaker said there is a commercial kitchen across the street at Heritage Hall that people rent.[[#2]] Planning said that without a deadline, the code would allow five years to build such a facility.[[#3]]
